title: AI-Driven Multi-Document Correlation for Financial Compliance - Varsha Shah, Independent
talk_summary: A financial-compliance research talk describing a three-part framework: graph-based entity correlation across documents, an adaptive probabilistic risk model that learns from audit outcomes, and cross-jurisdictional normalization. It reports strong detection metrics (91% precision, 87% recall, F1 0.89) and operational gains (76% fewer false positives, 40% less manual audit) on ~3M records across four jurisdictions.

takeaways.technique: Cross-artifact correlation instead of per-artifact validation
takeaways.what_they_do: They build a graph linking entities (employees, vendors, accounts, transactions, filings) across systems, then flag anomalies that only appear in the relationships, not in any single document.
takeaways.evidence_quote: many of today's most significant compliance and fraud risk exist between the documents, not within them
takeaways.numbers: 91% precision, 87% recall, F1 0.89; 76% false-positive reduction; ~40% less manual audit effort

takeaways.technique: Risk-score prioritization with learned weights from outcomes
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of static rules, they combine multiple risk indicators into a confidence-weighted score and retrain from confirmed-fraud and false-positive audit outcomes.

takeaways.technique: Precision/recall/F1 reporting on a labeled corpus
takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate the framework on ~3M records over 5 years across four jurisdictions and report precision, recall, F1, and operational deltas rather than anecdotes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these results produce a F1 score that is 0.89, indicating a strong balance between the precision and recall

takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated layer standardizes currencies, tax rules, reporting periods, and classification schemes so downstream risk scoring is consistent across jurisdictions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Without normalization, the same transaction can be interpreted differently depending on the jurisdiction
